5	/// The robot's two destructive maintenance actions: clearing the Hugging Face
6	/// cache and uninstalling every app.
7	///
8	/// A model rather than `@State` on the card, because the interesting part is not
9	/// the two calls but the rule in front of one of them — and that rule is worth
10	/// asserting without a view.
11	@MainActor
12	@Observable
13	final class MaintenanceModel {
14	    enum Action: Equatable, Identifiable, CaseIterable {
15	        case clearHuggingFaceCache
16	        case resetApps
17	
18	        var id: Self { self }
19	    }
20	
21	    /// What the confirmation dialog is asking about. Not `private(set)` — the
22	    /// dialog's binding writes it back on dismissal.
23	    var confirming: Action?
24	    private(set) var running: Action?
25	    /// The last action that finished cleanly, so the card can say so in place.
26	    private(set) var finished: Action?
27	    private(set) var lastError: String?
28	
29	    var isBusy: Bool {
30	        running != nil
31	    }
32	
33	    /// Uninstalling every app is `shutil.rmtree("/venvs/apps_venv/")`, and the
34	    /// daemon neither stops a running app first nor puts anything back — the
35	    /// interpreter a live app is executing in simply goes away underneath it.
36	    /// The robot offers no protection there, so this is the client's, and the
37	    /// card says which app to stop rather than only greying the button out.
38	    ///
39	    /// An unfamiliar process state counts as running, the same way
40	    /// `RobotAppStatus.State.isBusy` treats it: refusing to delete an
41	    /// environment that might be in use is the safe way to be wrong.
42	    func blockingApp(_ session: RobotSession) -> RobotApp? {
43	        guard let status = session.runningApp, status.isBusy else { return nil }
44	        return status.app
45	    }
46	
47	    func perform(_ action: Action, session: RobotSession) async {
48	        running = action
49	        finished = nil
50	        lastError = nil
51	        defer { running = nil }
52	        do {
53	            switch action {
54	            case .clearHuggingFaceCache: try await session.clearHuggingFaceCache()
55	            case .resetApps: try await session.resetApps()
56	            }
57	            finished = action
58	            // What the session last saw about installed apps is fiction now: the
59	            // venv every one of them lived in has just been deleted. Failing to
60	            // re-read is not worth reporting — the dock polls this anyway, and
61	            // the delete itself succeeded.
62	            if action == .resetApps {
63	                try? await session.refreshCurrentApp()
64	            }
65	        } catch {
66	            lastError.recordDaemonFailure(error)
67	        }
68	    }
69	}

## The localization catalogue

`Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` is the app's only catalogue, and `Localization.swift` is the only way in:
`.reachy("Wake up")` returns a `LocalizedStringResource` bound to `Bundle.module`.

It lives here because **both executables link this target**, so SwiftPM copies `ReachyMini_ReachyDesign.bundle` into
each — verified on a device build: `en.lproj/Localizable.strings` is present in `ReachySpike.app` _and_ in
`PlugIns/ReachyWidget.appex`. One catalogue, one hand-off to a translator, two processes served.

Three things measured rather than assumed:

- **`Section`, `LabeledContent`, `TextField` and `SecureField` only got their `LocalizedStringResource` initialiser in
  iOS 26 / macOS 26.** `Text`, `Button`, `Label`, `Toggle`, `Picker`, `navigationTitle`, `alert` and the rest have had
  one since iOS 16. `LocalizedControls.swift` backfills those four at this app's floor, forwarding to the
  `Text`-taking form. Both are visible against the iOS 26 SDK and the SDK's carries `@_disfavoredOverload`, so ours
  win with no ambiguity — 28 call sites that would otherwise each be a two-closure builder.
- **The catalogue derives a Swift symbol per key, and two keys that differ only in punctuation collide** — a hard
  build error from `xcstringstool`, not a warning. `"Bluetooth is switched off."` against `"Bluetooth is switched
  off"` was the app saying the same sentence two ways; `"Starting…"` against `"Starting"` was not, and the daemon's
  lifecycle took `"Starting up"` / `"Shutting down"` to clear it. Expect to be told when a new key rhymes with an old
  one, and fix the copy rather than the tooling.
- **`.xcstrings` compiles under the pinned swift.org toolchain**, unlike `#Preview`: SwiftPM shells out to `xcrun`
  for `xcstringstool`, so `mise run build` and `mise run test` are unaffected.

Seeding is manual. `SWIFT_EMIT_LOC_STRINGS` is not set for SwiftPM targets through Tuist, so Xcode never extracts:
the 335 keys with no interpolation were collected from the source and written in with `extractionState: "manual"`.
The ~50 keys that _do_ interpolate are deliberately absent — their stored form carries `%@` / `%lld` placeholders
whose types cannot be read off the call site, and a wrong entry is worse than a missing one, which merely falls back
to the English key. Finish them by opening the catalogue in Xcode, which extracts the placeholders correctly. The
working list lives under gitignored `.context/` and does not travel to another clone: rebuild it with

All seven ad-hoc sites now name a role: the viewport's three pieces of chrome (`.chrome`), the log console, the BLE

  `OnboardingFlow`, `BLEConsoleScreen`) needs its own `.ignoresSafeArea` when it adopts the role.

Every preview is now captured twice — `Apps/ReachyUISnapshotTests/PreviewTests.stencil` forks Prefire's built-in
test template and loops the capture over `[.light, .dark]`, naming the dark file with a `-dark` suffix. The light
names are untouched, which is why adopting it re-recorded nothing: 500 new files, 0 modified.

no equivalent of) and not as `\.colorScheme` in the environment (which moves SwiftUI's own colours and leaves

generated client can reach, and each is absent from the API for a different reason.

## An app's own settings

The daemon carries no route for an app's configuration. It reports a port — `AppInfo.extra["custom_app_url"]`,
regex-scraped out of the app's `main.py`, so it arrives as the app's *bind* address — and the app serves its own page
there; the conversation app logs `Serving settings UI from …/static` as it comes up. Until now that port was used for
one thing, reading `conversation.turn` off `/rpc`.

- **`AppSettingsScreen`** puts that page in a `WKWebView` — the only one in the app. A native screen could only be
  written against Conversation App 1.0's `/rpc` and would leave every other app with no settings at all. Hand-rolled
  representables rather than SwiftUI's `WebView`, which is iOS 26 / macOS 26 against this app's iOS 18 floor. The
  coordinator tracks `loadedURL` so a SwiftUI update does not reload a form someone is filling in, and a failed load
  goes through `RobotSession.message(for:)` — the one funnel that filters `NSURLErrorCancelled` and logs.
- **`RobotSession.appSettingsURL(for:)`** takes the app's port and the session's host, never the other way round
  (`0.0.0.0` dialled from a phone is the phone). Nil without a declared port, and nil for a relay session. **No
  fallback to 7860**, unlike `ConversationRPCClient`: a background stream nobody sees may guess, a row someone taps
  may not, and an absent key is the daemon's only signal that an app serves no page.
- **`RunningAppSheet`** adds `state == .running` and `isReachable` on top, because the process serving the page is the
  process that crashes — worst exactly when a bad setting is what took it down.

## Maintenance, and the guard the robot does not have

`/cache/clear-hf` and `/cache/reset-apps` mount at the app root under `--wireless-version`, like `/wifi/*` and
`/update/*`, so the committed spec (generated without the flag) does not carry them. Hand-written as
`CacheMaintenanceClient`, gated behind `canPerformMaintenance`.

**`reset-apps` is `shutil.rmtree("/venvs/apps_venv/")` and nothing else** — the daemon does not stop the running app
first, so its interpreter is deleted underneath it. `MaintenanceModel.blockingApp(_:)` refuses while an app is busy and
the card names the app to stop rather than only greying the button out. `RobotSession.resetApps()` also drops
`appCatalogueCache` and `installedAppsCache`, the same pair an install or a remove job drops: without that the Apps tab
went on offering Open and Remove on rows whose venv had just gone.

`WiFiSettingsCard` gains "Forget all" over `/wifi/forget_all` — one route rather than a loop over the rows, because the
per-network route answers 409 while another `nmcli` operation runs.

## The crash printed twice

`RobotAppStatus.error` is a stderr *tail* — the daemon's summary line plus the app's last lines — not the single
traceback line it was documented as. The sheet's State row inlined it under a two-line limit, so it read
`Process exited with code 1 / INFO: connection rejected (403 For…`: the opening of the very output printed in full two
rows below. `RunningAppCaption.label` now takes a `Failure`; the dock passes `.inline` because its one caption line is
the only place a crash can be read, the sheet passes `.shownSeparately`. The references never caught it because
`previewCrashed` was a single line, and a one-line tail renders identically whether a surface prints it once or twice.
It is a real multi-line tail now.
